fields.title: 📖 Ikhlāṣ – When is a deed accepted?
fields.body:
🖋️ **Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ** رحمه الله said about Allah’s words:

“That He may test you, which of you does the best deeds.” (Hūd 11:7)

“The **most sincere** and the **most correct** deeds.

If a deed is **sincere** but not correct, it is not accepted.

And if it is **correct** but not sincere, it is likewise not accepted, until it is sincere and correct.

It is sincere when it is done **for Allah**.

And it is correct when it **accords with the Sunnah**.”

🌙 **Conclusion:** A deed needs two basic conditions: **Ikhlāṣ** – the sincere intention for Allah alone – and **conformity with the Sunnah**.

immutable.source: Abū Nuʿaym, Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ, Bd. 8, S. 95; Ibn Abī ad-Dunyā, al-Ikhlāṣ wa-n-Niyyah, Nr. 22.
